## Motivation

On gfx950 (MI355X), DeepSeek-V4 decode with at most 8 query rows runs `swapab_attention`, which takes 12 to 14 µs per call. Its grid has only 2 to 60 programs, so one program's latency sets the call time. This PR cuts that latency and raises the router cap from 8 to 16 rows.

## Kernel architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["KV gather"] --> B["KV tile in LDS"] --> C["QK and PV MFMA"] --> D["O per PV tile"] --> E["combine_gfx950"]
```

- P stays in registers. PV runs in 8 tiles, and each tile's O stores right after its MFMAs. VGPR falls from 90 to 60.
- `combine_gfx950` loads `sink` and `pos` as scalars first and skips inverse RoPE on tiles without rope dims.
## What could break

- `_combine` is shared with SM100 and unchanged here. Only the gfx950 wrapper passes `combine_gfx950`. No SM100 GPU was available, so no test ran there. The sm_100 and sm_103 compiles match base.
- The aiter route's split reduce calls `inverse_rope_tail`, whose text and ISA match base.
- The buffer-load gather needs a cache of at most 2**31 - 2 bytes and an even page stride. Other caches keep global loads. A new test covers both edges.
- Rows 9 to 16 on gfx950 move from the aiter route to swap-AB.

## Correctness results

One MI355X, ROCm 7.2, triton 3.7.0.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Swap-AB unit tests, all 15 commits | pass; head 15 passed, 2 skipped (SM100-only) |
| Swap-AB, commit 13 vs head, 12 cases | bit-identical, 12 of 12 |
| Swap-AB, before and after, 12 cases | not bit-identical, max abs diff 0.016 |
| aiter route outputs, before and after, 16 cases | bit-identical, 16 of 16 |
| `_combine` (SM100 path), base vs head, 32 configs | bit-identical, same ISA, 32 of 32 |
| sm_100 compile, base vs commits 5 to 11, 96 configs | identical TTIR, PTX, SASS |
| GSM8K, 8-shot, 1319 questions, TP4, end to end | 0.952, gate 0.91, 0 invalid |

## Perf results

Base `60725d0e17` vs head `988525314c`. hipGraph device time in µs, median of 7 paired rounds. A step is 2 SWA calls plus 38 sparse calls.

### Cold

512 input copies, so KV misses L2 and the MALL. Step at bs 4, next_n 1: 529.4 to 316.5 µs (-40.2%), paired -213.0 µs, faster in 7 of 7 rounds.

| Layer | bs | next_n | Before µs [min, max] | After µs [min, max] | Change |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| swa | 1 | 1 | 11.78 [11.76, 11.84] | 6.78 [6.73, 6.83] | -42.4% |
| swa | 1 | 6 | 12.13 [12.10, 12.15] | 7.20 [7.19, 7.21] | -40.6% |
| swa | 4 | 1 | 12.04 [11.99, 12.06] | 7.09 [7.05, 7.16] | -41.1% |
| sparse | 1 | 1 | 12.94 [12.91, 12.96] | 7.01 [6.96, 7.16] | -45.8% |
| sparse | 1 | 6 | 14.42 [14.36, 14.49] | 9.17 [9.14, 9.24] | -36.4% |
| sparse | 4 | 1 | 13.30 [13.29, 13.34] | 7.96 [7.95, 7.98] | -40.2% |

### Warm

One input copy, so inputs stay in L2 and the MALL. Step: 476.1 to 277.9 µs (-41.6%), paired -197.7 µs, faster in 7 of 7 rounds.

| Layer | bs | next_n | Before µs [min, max] | After µs [min, max] | Change |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| swa | 1 | 1 | 11.05 [11.00, 11.10] | 6.21 [6.17, 6.26] | -43.8% |
| swa | 1 | 6 | 11.18 [11.16, 11.20] | 6.46 [6.45, 6.48] | -42.3% |
| swa | 4 | 1 | 10.98 [10.94, 11.01] | 6.20 [6.18, 6.24] | -43.5% |
| sparse | 1 | 1 | 11.49 [11.44, 11.52] | 6.26 [6.19, 6.44] | -45.5% |
| sparse | 1 | 6 | 13.05 [13.04, 13.07] | 8.23 [8.19, 8.24] | -36.9% |
| sparse | 4 | 1 | 11.95 [11.94, 12.03] | 6.99 [6.98, 7.02] | -41.5% |

### Router cap

Head only, cold, 7 runs. The aiter column is the faster of the image's aiter and aiter `main` `a1e5a46168`. Swap-AB is faster at every point, and its slowest run beats the fastest aiter run.

| Rows | Points (bs x next_n) | swa: swap-AB vs aiter µs | sparse: swap-AB vs aiter µs | Smallest margin µs (fastest aiter run minus slowest swap-AB run) |
|--:|---|---|---|--:|
| 9 | 9x1, 3x3 | 7.58 to 8.05 vs 10.40 to 10.59 | 11.21 to 12.78 vs 15.18 to 15.36 | 2.04 |
| 12 | 12x1, 4x3, 3x4, 2x6 | 7.35 to 7.92 vs 10.40 to 10.71 | 10.95 to 11.12 vs 14.47 to 14.66 | 2.44 |
| 16 | 16x1, 4x4 | 7.61 to 7.78 vs 10.12 to 10.44 | 12.85 to 12.87 vs 14.32 to 14.52 | 1.31 |

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with [pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). No changes.
- [x] Add [unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update [documentation](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). `SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND` now names the swap-AB route, in 988525314c.
- [x] Provide [accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed) results. GSM8K passes (correctness table). Speed is kernel-level only.
- [x] Follow the SGLang [code style guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

+# router row cap
+MAX_BATCH = 16
+
+# d rows one PV step covers: 4 warps x one 16-row MFMA tile
+PV_TILE = gl.constexpr(64)
+
+
+@gluon.jit
+def _load_v4_hip(
+    CACHE,
+    ids,
+    valid,
+    PAGE: gl.constexpr,
+    STRIDE: gl.constexpr,
+    KV_LAYOUT: gl.constexpr,
+    DATA_BYTES: gl.constexpr,
+    SCALE_BYTES: gl.constexpr,
+    TILE: gl.constexpr,
+):
+    d = gl.arange(0, 512, gl.SliceLayout(0, KV_LAYOUT))
+    base = (ids // PAGE).to(gl.int64)[:, None] * STRIDE
+    slot = (ids % PAGE)[:, None]
+    mask = valid[:, None] & (d[None, :] < 448)
+    bits = gl.load(CACHE + base + slot * DATA_BYTES + d[None, :], mask, 0)
+    exponent = gl.load(
+        CACHE + base + PAGE * DATA_BYTES + slot * SCALE_BYTES + d[None, :] // TILE,
+        mask,
+        0,
+    )
+    nope = gl.amd.cdna4.scaled_upcast(
+        bits.to(gl.float8e4nv, bitcast=True), exponent, gl.bfloat16
+    )
+    # a uint8 pointer splits the rope into 2-byte masked loads; bf16-typed it
+    # stays one 16-byte load per thread
+    rope_ptr = (CACHE + base + slot * DATA_BYTES + 448).to(
+        gl.pointer_type(gl.bfloat16)
+    ) + (d[None, :] - 448)
+    rope = gl.load(rope_ptr, valid[:, None] & (d[None, :] >= 448), 0)
+    return gl.where(d[None, :] < 448, nope, rope)
+
+
+# a buffer descriptor's num_records (Triton sets 2**31 - 2 bytes); a cache past it
+# keeps the global-load path, whose offsets are 64-bit
+BUFFER_BYTES = gl.constexpr(2**31 - 2)
+
+
+@gluon.jit
+def _load_v4_buffer(
+    CACHE,
+    ids,
+    valid,
+    PAGE: gl.constexpr,
+    STRIDE: gl.constexpr,
+    KV_LAYOUT: gl.constexpr,
+    DATA_BYTES: gl.constexpr,
+    SCALE_BYTES: gl.constexpr,
+    TILE: gl.constexpr,
+):
+    # an invalid row's offsets start at 2**31, past num_records, so the hardware reads
+    # 0. Columns >= 448 of the fp8 and scale loads read the row's own rope and pad
+    # bytes, which the final select drops.
+    d = gl.arange(0, 512, gl.SliceLayout(0, KV_LAYOUT))
+    page = (ids // PAGE) * STRIDE
+    slot = ids % PAGE
+    row = gl.where(valid, page + slot * DATA_BYTES, -(2**31))[:, None]
+    bits = gl.amd.cdna4.buffer_load(CACHE, row + d[None, :])
+    scales = gl.where(valid, page + PAGE * DATA_BYTES + slot * SCALE_BYTES, -(2**31))
+    exponent = gl.amd.cdna4.buffer_load(CACHE, scales[:, None] + d[None, :] // TILE)
+    nope = gl.amd.cdna4.scaled_upcast(
+        bits.to(gl.float8e4nv, bitcast=True), exponent, gl.bfloat16
+    )
+    # a masked-off vector also reads 0: with `other` unset Triton adds no select
+    rope = gl.amd.cdna4.buffer_load(
+        CACHE.to(gl.pointer_type(gl.bfloat16)),
+        (row >> 1) + (d[None, :] - 224),
+        (d >= 448)[None, :],
+    )
+    return gl.where(d[None, :] < 448, nope, rope)
+
+
+@gluon.jit
+def _load_kv(
+    CACHE,
+    ids,
+    valid,
+    TOKENS: gl.constexpr,
+    PAGE: gl.constexpr,
+    STRIDE: gl.constexpr,
+    KV_LAYOUT: gl.constexpr,
+    DATA_BYTES: gl.constexpr,
+    SCALE_BYTES: gl.constexpr,
+    TILE: gl.constexpr,
+):
+    # the rope offsets count bf16 elements, so a row must start on an even byte
+    if TOKENS // PAGE * STRIDE <= BUFFER_BYTES and STRIDE % 2 == 0:
+        return _load_v4_buffer(
+            CACHE, ids, valid, PAGE, STRIDE, KV_LAYOUT, DATA_BYTES, SCALE_BYTES, TILE
+        )
+    else:
+        return _load_v4_hip(
+            CACHE, ids, valid, PAGE, STRIDE, KV_LAYOUT, DATA_BYTES, SCALE_BYTES, TILE
+        )
+
+
+@gluon.jit
+def _load_q(
+    Q, QS: gl.constexpr, QH: gl.constexpr, H: gl.constexpr, Q_LAYOUT: gl.constexpr
+):
+    qh = gl.arange(0, H, gl.SliceLayout(1, Q_LAYOUT))
+    qd = gl.arange(0, 512, gl.SliceLayout(0, Q_LAYOUT))
+    return gl.load(Q + gl.program_id(0) * QS + qh[:, None] * QH + qd[None, :])

+def rope_tables(
+    d, FREQS, pos, freq_stride, HEAD_DIM: tl.constexpr, ROPE_DIM: tl.constexpr

+    cos = tl.load(FREQS + pos * freq_stride + freq_index, is_rope, 0)
+    sin = tl.load(FREQS + pos * freq_stride + freq_index + 1, is_rope, 0)

+        base = torch.empty(bt, 512, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+        fused = torch.empty_like(base)
+        load_both[(1,)](
+            raw, ids, valid.to(torch.int8), base, fused, page, stride, bt, num_warps=4
+        )
+
+        a, b = base.view(torch.int16), fused.view(torch.int16)
+        both_nan = base.isnan() & fused.isnan()
+        bad = (a != b) & ~both_nan
+        self.assertEqual(int(bad.sum()), 0, f"{int(bad.sum())} of {bad.numel()} differ")
+        self.assertTrue(bool(valid.any()) and bool((~valid).any()))
+        self.assertTrue(bool(base[~valid].eq(0).all()))
+
+    def test_serving_exponents(self):
+        self.check(100, 150, 1)
+
+    def test_wide_exponents(self):
+        self.check(1, 255, 2)
+
+    def test_zero_exponent(self):
+        self.check(0, 1, 3)
+
+
+def launch_combine(combine, b, nt, bd, rope_dim, inputs):
+    part, mx, den, sink, freqs, positions = inputs
+    out = torch.empty((b, 16, 512), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+    combine[(b, 16, 512 // bd)](
+        part,
+        mx,
+        den,
+        sink,
+        out,
+        freqs,
+        positions,
+        FREQ_STRIDE=freqs.stride(0),
+        ROPE_DIM=rope_dim,
+        NT=nt,
+        ST=triton.next_power_of_2(nt),
+        H=16,
+        BD=bd,
+        num_warps=4,
+    )
+    return out
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(
+    torch.cuda.is_available() and is_hip() and is_gfx95_supported(), "requires gfx950"
+)
+class TestSwapABCombineRopeTiles(CustomTestCase):
+    def check(self, b, nt, bd, rope_dim, sink_values=None, seed=0):
+        self.assertEqual((512 - rope_dim) % bd, 0)
+        gen = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(seed)
+        part = torch.randn(b, nt, 16, 512, device="cuda", generator=gen) * 8
+        part[torch.rand(part.shape, device="cuda", generator=gen) < 0.1] = 0
+        mx = torch.randn(b, nt, 16, device="cuda", generator=gen) * 3
+        den = torch.rand(b, nt, 16, device="cuda", generator=gen)
+        den[torch.rand(den.shape, device="cuda", generator=gen) < 0.2] = 0
+        sink = torch.randn(16, device="cuda", generator=gen)
+        if sink_values is not None:
+            sink[: len(sink_values)] = torch.tensor(sink_values, device="cuda")
+        angles = torch.randn(64, rope_dim // 2, device="cuda", generator=gen)
+        freqs = torch.stack((angles.cos(), angles.sin()), dim=-1).flatten(1)
+        freqs[:, :4] = torch.tensor([1.0, 0.0, 0.0, -1.0], device="cuda")
+        positions = torch.randint(0, 64, (b,), device="cuda", generator=gen)
+        inputs = (part, mx, den, sink, freqs, positions)
+        tiled = launch_combine(combine_gfx950, b, nt, bd, rope_dim, inputs)
+        generic = launch_combine(_combine, b, nt, bd, rope_dim, inputs)
+        self.assertTrue(
+            torch.equal(tiled.view(torch.int16), generic.view(torch.int16)),
+            f"b={b} nt={nt} bd={bd} rope_dim={rope_dim}",
+        )
+
+    def test_bit_identical(self):
+        for rope_dim in (64, 128):
+            for b, nt, bd in [(1, 4, 64), (4, 20, 64), (3, 17, 64), (4, 5, 128)]:
+                if (512 - rope_dim) % bd == 0:
+                    self.check(b, nt, bd, rope_dim, seed=b + nt)
+
+    def test_inf_sinks(self):
+        self.check(
+            2, 9, 64, 64, sink_values=[float("inf"), float("-inf"), 0.0, 1e4], seed=5
+        )
+
+
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     unittest.main()
